newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases state grip on satellite use, ownership.
newsitem.headline: India eases state grip on satellite use, ownership.

text.p: India on Thursday ended its state monopoly on satellite usage and ownership, allowing private firms to use transponders on state satellites and permiting private users to establish commercial communications satellites.

"Operations from Indian soil will be allowed with both Indian and foreign satellites in accordance with norms and conditions to be evolved but Indian satellites will be accorded preferential treatment," a government statement said.
It said Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet had approved a policy framework to strengthen and regulate an orderly growth of satellite communications systems in India.

"With this far-reaching decision of the cabinet, in the next few months the government will work out the norms and conditions concerning the various aspects of the policy for its effective implementation," the statement said without elaborating.

"It is expected that the enunciation of the policy framework will lead to the development of a healthy and thriving communications satellite and ground equipment industry as well as satellite communications service industry in India," it said.
